root.name: King's Indian Defense: Semi-Classical Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. Nf3 O-O 5. e3 d6 6. Be2

overview: White chooses a modest set-up with e3 and Be2 instead of the big e4 centre. The usual game goes 6...Nbd7 7.O-O e5, after which White can exchange on e5 for a calm position or play b4 and queenside space. Black can also strike with ...c5 or ...Nc6 (Hollywood). It is a quieter White try that gives Black an easy game if White drifts.

white_ideas.idea: Castle, play Qc2 and Rd1, then either dxe5 or hold the d4 pawn.
Queenside expansion with b4 and c5 against the ...e5 set-up.

black_ideas.idea: ...Nbd7 and ...e5, then ...exd4 or ...Re8 for a Hedgehog-like game.
...c5 or ...c6 to restrain the centre and challenge d4.

typical_structures.structure: After dxe5 dxe5 a symmetrical-ish open d-file with Black's g7 bishop strong.
d4 against e5 with tension, no locked centre until a later d5.

character.notes: Many branches (Exchange, Hollywood, Benoni-type c5) are positional, not mutual attacks; lacks the Classical race.

soundness.notes: Fully sound and reputable for both sides.

structure.notes: Centre often unresolved: d4 vs ...e5 tension or an exchange; not locked.

approach.notes: Ordinary KID branch, played by strong players as a sideline.

level.notes: Black needs to know the KID plans; theory is lighter than the Classical.

sublines_that_differ.name: Queenside Storm Line
sublines_that_differ.how: White gains queenside space; sharper race than the exchange line.

character.reason: Exchange and positional lines dominate; neither forcing nor especially hard to crack.

structure.reason: d4 against ...e5 stays in tension or is exchanged, not locked.

approach.reason: Played by strong players as a regular KID line.

level.reason: Black needs KID plan knowledge but lines are quiet and little theory.

plans.reason: Black's g7 bishop on the long diagonal defines the middlegame.
